# GuardDog exact-lock investigation

**Draft, blocking and not merge-ready.** Supported hosted execution has been proven, but this is not yet an accepted complete malicious-dependency gate. Findings and remaining blockers are documented in [the investigation](guarddog-findings-2026-10-26.md). No historical WHOIS exceptions were imported. Missing capability never means a false positive.

## Isolation and disclosure

- GuardDog 3.2.0 and nono-py 0.16.0 use a complete hash-required, wheel-only CPython 3.12 Linux x86-64 lock. Fresh virtual environments; no sdist builds or package lifecycle execution. Pip uses `--isolated --disable-pip-version-check --no-cache-dir --require-hashes --only-binary=:all:`. No supported GuardDog optional telemetry switch was found; none is invented.
- The pinned-action Ubuntu 24.04 job has only `contents: read`, checkout credentials are not persisted, and scanner/controller receive a clean explicit environment without tokens. Native `is_supported()` must pass before GuardDog imports or dependency downloads. There is no sandbox bypass or compatibility fallback.
- **Important admission correction:** initial hosted runs through d4e6795 used nono's default `auto`, which is Landlock-first. The actual proof covered TCP/filesystem restrictions, **not UDP**; DNS requests were not ruled out. Current code explicitly requests supported `enforcement_mode="seccomp"`, layering Landlock and static UDP/raw-socket/io_uring restrictions. Its prerequisite must prove allowed synthetic file I/O plus forbidden read/write, TCP connection and IPv4/IPv6 UDP creation. Never infer complete network denial from earlier TCP-only results.
- Bootstrap necessarily contacts PyPI (`pypi.org`, wheel delivery `files.pythonhosted.org`) with scanner dependency names/versions. Pinned actions and checkout use GitHub infrastructure. The controlled downloader makes only credential-free HTTPS GETs to `registry.npmjs.org` for public package metadata and exact locked archives, without redirects or proxy inheritance. No dependency name/version is sent to DataDog/GuardDog SaaS. No application source, secrets, raw scanner report or binary is uploaded. Public Actions logs contain sanitized finding identities/hashes, not private evidence.
- GuardDog initialization attempts optional popularity refreshes, including unrelated ecosystems. Bundled caches are copied unchanged into the private worker; no timestamps are fabricated. With the stronger prerequisite proven, attempted refresh traffic is denied before leaving the sandbox. Stale popularity data is not used for an accepted verdict.

## Exact bytes, complete inventory and hard failures

The controller enumerates every lock-v3 archive, including development, transitive, aliases and all optional/platform packages. It rejects nonregistry URLs, links, bundled entries and nonexact versions. Every SHA512 SRI is checked before archive parsing and rechecked inside the worker. No selector is resolved and no npm installation occurs. Native `guarddog npm verify` re-resolves package.json and is deliberately not used as an exact-lock shortcut.

Native `safe_extract` and `Analyzer` execute inside `nono_py.sandboxed_exec`, the pre-exec mechanism used by GuardDog's own extraction sandbox, with stronger explicit seccomp mode. Archive preflight refuses links, devices, traversal, mixed roots and duplicates. It bounds files (20,000), compressed bytes (128 MiB), extracted bytes (512 MiB), and compression ratio (100). Each worker gets 180 seconds wall time, 120 CPU seconds, 512 MiB per output file, 256 descriptors and 2 GiB address space. Controller concurrency is two, with 2 GiB address space/1800 CPU seconds and a 2400-second outer timeout. The native process-count limit is 16 **RLIMIT_NPROC**, a per-UID/best-effort limit, not a claim of a dedicated cgroup process-tree boundary. No package code is invoked; the synthetic lifecycle sentinel must remain absent.

Metadata responses are capped at 64 MiB; downloads have 30-second socket and 90-second read deadlines. A bounded eight-entry metadata memoization cache avoids repeated simultaneous package metadata requests. All native 54 source rules and each active metadata rule must return the exact expected inventory without errors. Missing, failed, malformed or unclassified metadata results fail closed. Native source-rule path selectors/comment filtering/max-hit semantics remain unchanged; this is not a claim that every byte is classified.

### Versioned DefinitelyTyped root adapter

The actual `@types/node@24.19.2` SRI-bound archive root is `node v24.19`, which native metadata lookup does not recognize. Only `@types/*` roots exactly matching their locked major.minor line may be renamed inside the private extraction to the native unscoped-name root. The manifest must first match exact package name/version. No file bytes change; hashes remain bound to the original archive and findings are mapped back to original paths. Hosted synthetic positive analysis compares native results on the ordinary named root and this normalized root, and must be identical. This is an explicit adapter, not an upstream-native coverage claim.

## Coverage still requires a decision

`.github/security/guarddog.json` is `review-required`. Active source/metadata scans and exact expiring finding reviews do **not** override these unresolved native capabilities:

1. Two WHOIS rules require domain metadata. Native failures/missing dates may become a clean result; a reliable bounded public metadata adapter and equivalence tests have not been accepted. [ICANN ended most gTLD WHOIS obligations in 2025](https://www.icann.org/en/announcements/details/icann-update-launching-rdap-sunsetting-whois-27-01-2025-en), not every WHOIS service.
2. `typosquatting`: the native [npm-rank latest release](https://github.com/tristan-f-r/npm-rank/releases/tag/latest) and raw.json asset are dated 2024-11-27. Downloading it today is not a current ranking. No fake-fresh timestamp or stale-data clean verdict is accepted.
3. `risky_new_dependency`: native history comparison re-resolves selectors and launches recursive subprocess scans. Scanning all actual locked transitive archives is useful but not semantically identical to that historical rule. An exact-lock history/risk join would be an explicit adaptation requiring separate validation.

False-positive and expected-behavior reviews match exact name/version/SRI/all lock paths/rule/capability/file/line/context hash. Each has an explanation, owner, hashed evidence document and expiry within 30 days. Changed, expired, duplicate, broad or stale/unused exceptions fail. Unavailable capabilities cannot be excepted. Binary presence and the Lefthook provenance regression remain unwaived. The job therefore remains red even after successful active-rule coverage; a green prerequisite is never advertised as a clean dependency scan.

Official sources checked 2026-10-26: [GuardDog 3.2.0](https://github.com/DataDog/guarddog/releases/tag/v3.2.0), [sandbox](https://github.com/DataDog/guarddog/blob/v3.2.0/guarddog/sandbox.py), [npm resolver](https://github.com/DataDog/guarddog/blob/v3.2.0/guarddog/scanners/npm_project_scanner.py), [nono 0.16.0](https://github.com/nolabs-ai/nono-py/releases/tag/v0.16.0). The installed hash-locked native API documents the seccomp mode and resource-limit semantics; actual hosted proof is required before acceptance.
